objective: metric round 2, with the measured failures of round 1 in the prompt

metrics.title: Hyperbolic reference-affinity cone coverage of the SID prefix tree
metrics.formula:
Let each item i have SID (c1,c2,c3), c_l in {0,...,255}, L=3. Build the prefix tree T (root at depth 0; node = prefix (c1..cd)).
EMBEDDING (deterministic, no fitted values). For a node v at depth d(v), set radius r(v)=ln(1+d(v)), and angular coordinate theta(v) by recursive equal-sector subdivision: the root's 256 children take theta = 2*pi*k/256 (k=c1); each child's 256 children split the parent's sector of width 2*pi/256 into 256 equal sub-sectors (k=c2); and so on. Item i sits at
  x_i = exp_0( r(v_i) * (cos theta_i, sin theta_i) ) = tanh(r(v_i)/2) * (cos theta_i, sin theta_i)
in the open unit disk (Poincare ball, curvature K=-1).
HYPERBOLIC DISTANCE: d_H(u,v) = arcosh( 1 + 2|u-v|^2 / ((1-|u|^2)(1-|v|^2)) ).
REFERENCE AFFINITY: from the frozen Issue #126 reference take, for every TRAIN item q, its source representation s_q, and for every item j its target representation t_j. Define A(q) = the m=10 items j != q with largest cosine(s_q, t_j) (m=10 is derived: it is the Recall@10 budget; ties broken by ascending item index).
HYPERBOLIC FRECHET MEAN: b_q = Karcher mean in the ball of {x_j : j in A(q)}, by the fixed-point iteration b <- exp_b( (1/m) * sum_j log_b(x_j) ), 10 iterations from b = x_q, using the closed-form Poincare exp/log maps.
COVERAGE RADIUS: R_q = max_{j in A(q)} d_H(b_q, x_j).
PER-SOURCE SCORE: g_q = d_H(b_q, 0) / ( d_H(b_q, 0) + R_q )   (in (0,1]; equals 1 iff the cone is a single point).

metrics.title: Training-pair hit rate of a curvature −1 beam-10 shortest-geodesic-path reader over the SID trie.
metrics.formula:
Let N items, L levels, K = 256, and sid_i = (q_{i,1},…,q_{i,L}) be the exported integer code tuple of item i. Let p = (q_1,…,q_ℓ) denote a prefix and P(p) = { i : sid_i[1..ℓ] = p }. Prefix set S_ℓ = { p : |P(p)| > 0 }. Write x^s_i, x^t_i in the unit Poincaré ball B = {x in R^d : ‖x‖<1} for the frozen reference source and target representations z^s_i, z^t_i (temperature tau stored with the reference; tau := 1 if absent), with one scalar scale
  sigma = 1 / Quantile_0.99( ‖tau*z^t_i‖_2 , i = 1..N ),  and  x_i = tanh( sigma*tau*‖z_i‖ ) * z_i/‖z_i‖   (x_i = 0 if z_i = 0).
Both source and target maps use the same sigma and tau. Poincaré metric with c = 1: Möbius addition u⊕v = ((1+2<u,v>+‖v‖²)u + (1−‖u‖²)v) / (1+2<u,v>+‖u‖²‖v‖²), and d(u,v) = 2*artanh( ‖(−u)⊕v‖ ) with (−u)⊕v the Möbius sum. Fréchet barycentre of a prefix, b_p = argmin_{b in B} Σ_{i in P(p)} d(b, x^t_i)², computed by the Karcher fixed point b ← exp_b( (1/|P(p)|) Σ_{i in P(p)} log_b(x^t_i) ), initialised at the member with smallest ‖x^t_i‖, 50 iterations, stopped when ‖mean tangent‖ < 1e-10, where log_b(x) = (2/lambda_b)*artanh(‖(−b)⊕x‖)*((−b)⊕x)/‖(−b)⊕x‖, lambda_b = 2/(1−‖b‖²), and exp_b(w) = b ⊕ ( tanh(lambda_b‖w‖/2) * w/‖w‖ ). If |P(p)| = 1 then b_p = x^t of that member.
Path score of a code path q = (q_1..q_ℓ) for a query source s:
  S(q; s) = d(x^s_s, b_{q_1}) + Σ_{m=2..ℓ} d(b_{q_1..q_{m−1}}, b_{q_1..q_m}).
Beam reader with width B = 10 (B is the recall cutoff k = 10, nothing else): level 1 candidates = S_1 ranked by S, keep the best 10 (ties broken by lexicographically smaller code tuple). For m = 2..L expand each kept prefix by its children in S_m, rank by S, keep the best 10. Since every increment for m >= 2 is independent of s, the best-B children of a parent are exactly its B geodesically nearest children; this pruning is exact by the triangle inequality, so no path that could enter the global top-10 is ever dropped. Reading stops at level L with a set R(s) of at most 10 full code tuples.
For each training pair (s,t) with s != t: hit(s,t) = 1 if sid_t ∈ R(s), else 0. Let Q be the training-pair list in file order, skipped to at most 20000 pairs by taking every ceil(|Q|/20000)-th pair. METRIC = (1/|Q'|) * Σ_{(s,t) in Q'} hit(s,t), a number in [0,1], higher better.
metrics.inputs: the exported Stage-2 SID table (integer array sid[N, L], values in 0..K−1); the TRAINING split list of (source_item_id, target_item_id) pairs; the frozen Issue #126 reference arrays Zsrc[N, d] and Ztgt[N, d] with its stored scalar temperature. Nothing else — no recall value, no Stage-3 artefact, no validation or test pair.
metrics.geometry: fixed curvature c = 1 (unit negative curvature; no tuned curvature). Curvature enters in three load-bearing places: (1) the exponential map at the origin, x = exp_0(tau*sigma*z) = tanh(‖.‖) * unit vector, so reference vectors become points of a ball of radius < 1 rather than plane vectors; (2) every prefix representative b_p is a Karcher/Fréchet barycentre, i.e. the minimiser of summed squared GEODESIC distance, which in a curved ball sits strictly closer to the origin than the Euclidean mean and is not obtainable by averaging coordinates; (3) the decoder's score is a sum of geodesic lengths, and hyperbolic distance diverges as points approach the boundary, so the level-1 term and the deep increments are weighted by the geometry, not by a linear scale. Consequence: taking c -> 0 changes both the barycentres and the relative size of the increments, hence changes the induced ordering of tables — this is not a Euclidean distance in disguise.
metrics.why: Stage-3 Recall@10 is literally "did the true SID survive a competition in which at most 10 SID sequences are kept". This metric reproduces that decision with a parameter-free curved reader and reports how often the truth survives. So it measures the headroom the table itself grants: a table with separable, geodesically tight prefixes and non-degenerate deep splits leaves the target's SID among the 10 shortest paths from the source; a table whose prefixes cut across the reference geometry does not, whatever ideal reader is used. What it adds over Q_H: (i) Q_H is a level-1 prefix rank and collapses at level 2 (+0.287) because a near-singleton prefix makes the rank degenerate, whereas here every level contributes a genuine geodesic increment b_parent -> b_child, so all L levels are priced jointly without degeneracy; (ii) it rewards tight hierarchical refinement (small increments) and punishes wasted depth (random deeper codes put a child barycentre far from its parent, inflating every path through that branch, which the beam punishes), the quantity that decides whether the search can travel to depth L without losing the truth; (iii) it carries the aliasing ceiling for free — two items with the same full SID are one candidate, so a target can never be "hit twice", which prefix counts cannot see; (iv) it is aggregated, ordinal and scale-free with a 10-slot competition, i.e. the same regime that made Q_H work, unlike the local per-pair margins that failed.
metrics.compute: barycentres for at most L*N ~ 1e5 prefixes cost sum_p |P(p)| * 50 = 50*L*N ~ 5e6 point updates, vectorised by level, a few seconds; the trie has at most L*N edges so edge geodesic distances number ~1e5 and are computed once; per training pair only the K = 256 level-1 Poincaré distances are computed (2e4 * 256 = 5.1e6), every level-2+ increment being a precomputed lookup, and the beam is at most L*10*10 arithmetic steps per pair. Total 5-15 s single-core on 24587 items and 256 codes.
metrics.risks: if the reference's target representations are near-degenerate, all prefix barycentres collapse to one point, the level-1 term becomes constant and the metric saturates near 10/N for every table, giving no dynamic range across the 97 pairs; because the pairs are training pairs and the reference was fitted on them, the metric can look uniformly good and compress differences; Karcher iteration can converge slowly for prefixes whose members sit near the boundary (mitigated by the fixed 50-iteration cap and the deterministic initialisation); the surrogate reader is ideal, so it prices sequence length only through geodesic increments and under-penalises a table with perfect coarse alignment plus useless but geometrically cheap deep splits; deterministic tie-breaking must be applied or the value is implementation-dependent.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on the semantically blind table sid_i = ( i mod K, floor(i/K) mod K, floor(i/K²) mod K, … ), unique and perfectly balanced: every level-1 bucket is a uniform random sample of the item set, so all 256 barycentres sit on top of the global barycentre, d(x^s_s, b_{q_1}) is identical across candidates up to sampling noise, and every path increment is drawn from one common distribution; the top-10 is then decided by noise and the hit rate tends to about 10 times the largest SID multiplicity over N, i.e. the floor. Correctly it should be near the floor for Stage 3 as well, but any table with a good level-1 and useless deep splits is where it will most over-predict.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic tree-conditional softmax log-likelihood of the SID path under the frozen behaviour reference
metrics.formula:
Let the table have N items, L levels and alphabet size V (V=256). Item i owns the code path c_i=(c_i1,...,c_iL), c_il in {1..V}. A prefix q is a tuple (q_1..q_k); q=() is the root. Children(q)={c : q^(c) is a prefix of at least one item}, where ^ is concatenation. Let T be the training interaction set. Let tau>0 be the reference's own softmax temperature and let K>0 be the reference's own curvature magnitude. Rescale every reference vector by sqrt(K) so the working ball has unit curvature (-1); after this no curvature constant remains in the computation.

Poincare distance on the unit ball:
  d(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2*||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)*(1-||y||^2)) ).
Lorentz barycentre of a finite set S of ball points (closed form, no iteration):
  z(x) = ( (1+||x||^2)/(1-||x||^2) , 2x/(1-||x||^2) ) in R^{1+d},
  Z = sum_{x in S} z(x),
  zbar = Z / sqrt(-<Z,Z>_L),  <u,v>_L = -u_0 v_0 + sum_j u_j v_j,
  m(S) = ( zbar_1..zbar_d ) / ( 1 + zbar_0 ).
For every non-root node q^(c) with item set S(q,c)={i : c_i starts with q^(c)}, define its prototype
  mu(q,c) = m( { x_i : i in S(q,c) } ),
where x_i is the reference's frozen target representation of item i (learned on training pairs only).
For a training pair (u,i) in T, let s_u be the frozen source representation of source u and let q_l=(c_i1..c_i,l-1). The per-level conditional log-probability of the true child is
  g_l(u,i) = logit(q_l, c_il) - logsumexp_{c in Children(q_l)} logit(q_l, c),
  logit(q,c) = - d(s_u, mu(q,c)) / tau.
If |Children(q_l)|=1 the term is exactly 0. The metric is
  M = (1/|T|) * sum_{(u,i) in T} sum_{l=1..L} g_l(u,i).
M is one scalar; larger (less negative) is better.
metrics.geometry: The space is the Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature (curvature -1 after rescaling the reference's K); all quantities are intrinsic hyperbolic quantities. Curvature enters twice: (a) the logits are negative Poincare geodesic distances d(s_u, mu(q,c))/tau, and (b) each prototype is a Lorentz/hyperboloid barycentre, i.e. an average in the Lorentz model projected back to the ball, not a Euclidean mean. The tree-conditional softmax is defined on distances measured with the curved metric; the same formula with Euclidean ||s_u - mu|| would be a different number. No tangent-space Euclidean shortcut is used.
metrics.why: Stage-3 recall@10 is the probability that beam search over the SID trie keeps the target's token path. This metric is exactly the log-likelihood that a source assigns to that path under a tree-conditional hyperbolic classifier: at every prefix the model must put mass on the true next code among the codes that actually exist under that prefix. It therefore measures, level by level and conditional on the parent, whether items that share the parent prefix are behaviourally close enough for the reference to prefer the true child. Q_H scores the level-1 prefix globally and degrades at levels 2-3 because those prefixes become nearly item identifiers; here a parent with one child contributes 0, so near-unique deeper codes cannot inflate or collapse the score, while genuinely branching deeper levels contribute their true conditional log-loss. Compared with Q_H it adds (i) per-parent conditioning, i.e. refinement quality rather than global coarse separation, (ii) a proper normalisation by the number of competing siblings, so tables with different branching are comparable, and (iii) curvature-aware bucket prototypes, so the score is not a prefix count or a same-bucket ratio. It is not a margin (hyp_voronoi_margin_l1) and not an R^2 of distances (hyp_adj_r2_l1).
metrics.compute: With N=24587 items, L levels and V=256 codes: one pass over items builds the trie and accumulates the hyperboloid lifts, O(N*L*d). Each node prototype is one O(|S|*d) sum plus one renormalisation, total O(N*L*d) over all nodes per level. Each training pair needs, at each level, distances to the siblings of its own path, so the cost is O(|T|*L*B) with B the mean branching factor of the nodes visited (B<=V=256; typically a few tens at the root and much less below). There is no matrix of all item pairs. On 24587 items and 256 codes this is seconds to well under a minute with a single vectorised numpy pass, and O(N*L) memory plus the reference arrays.
metrics.risks:
- The formula assumes source and target representations live in one shared Poincare ball, which is what a two-tower Issue #126 reference normally provides; if they live in two different balls the metric is undefined and needs the reference's fixed alignment.
- Training pairs are in-sample for the reference, so absolute values are optimistic; this is harmless for ranking 97 tables because the same frozen reference is used for all, but it can compress between-table variance.
- If the reference's tau or K is misreported, or if item representations are dominated by a few hub items, prototypes and logits shift.
- Very shallow tables (L=1) reduce M to a level-1 term; very unbalanced tables can have almost all deeper terms equal to 0, leaving only the root term.
- Numerical guards are needed (clamp ||x|| <= 1-1e-7; logsumexp in the log domain), and if the reference ball is very close to the boundary the barycentre sum can be ill-conditioned.
metrics.failure_mode: It must be worst on the table obtained by assigning level-1 codes uniformly at random, independently of behaviour, and then making every deeper level deterministic (each parent has exactly one child, e.g. c_i2..c_iL encode the item index). Such a table has maximal apparent "fine structure" but no behavioural information: every deeper g_l is 0 by construction, the level-1 prototypes are random mixtures of unrelated items, and the true child prototype is far from s_u relative to random siblings, so M is strongly negative even though prefix counts and branching look fine. A second worst case is an anti-clustered table that deliberately puts the behaviourally most distant items under the same level-1 code while keeping high branching at every level.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic leave-one-out conditional SID code log-probability (per token).
metrics.formula:
Notation. N items; L SID levels; C = 256 codes per level. For item i the integer code at level l is c_l(i) in {0..255}; the level-l prefix is pi_l(i) = (c_1(i),...,c_l(i)); the parent prefix is par_l(i) = pi_{l-1}(i) for l>=2. The frozen reference gives, per item, a source vector u_i and a target vector v_i in the open ball B_R^d = {x in R^d : ||x|| < R}. Curvature magnitude c = 1/R^2 (sectional curvature K = -c); R is the reference's stored ball radius (R=1 if absent). Everything is deterministic.

(1) Poincare distance (curvature -c):
    d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * arcosh( 1 + 2c*||x-y||^2 / ((1-c*||x||^2)(1-c*||y||^2)) ).

(2) Moebius sum and the Riemannian log/exp maps used by (4):
    x (+) y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2)x + (1-c||x||^2)y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2).
    exp_x(v) = x (+) ( tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||/2) * v/(sqrt(c)*||v||) ),  exp_x(0)=x.
    log_x(y) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh( sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y|| ) * ((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||,  log_x(x)=0.

(3) Prototype of each prefix. For every level l and every prefix pi present in the table, G_pi = { i : pi_l(i) = pi }, n_pi = |G_pi|, and B_pi is the hyperbolic Frechet (Karcher) barycentre B_pi = argmin_x sum_{i in G_pi} d_c(x, v_i)^2, computed by the fixed-point iteration x <- exp_x( (1/n_pi) * sum_{i in G_pi} log_x(v_i) ), initialised at x0 = the member of G_pi with smallest d_c(0, v_i), stopped when ||(1/n_pi) sum log_x(v_i)|| < 1e-7 or at 100 iterations. B_empty = Karcher barycentre of all v_i.

(4) Leave-one-out own prototype. For the pair (i,l) with pi = pi_l(i):
    if n_pi >= 2:  q_{i,l} = exp_{B_pi}( - log_{B_pi}(v_i) / (n_pi - 1) )   (exact first-order Riemannian LOO mean, since sum_{j in G_pi} log_{B_pi}(v_j) = 0 at the Karcher fixed point);
    if n_pi = 1 and l >= 2:  q_{i,l} = B_{par_l(i)}  (the parent's prototype);
    if n_pi = 1 and l = 1:   q_{i,l} = B_empty.

(5) Sibling class set at (i,l). For l = 1: S_{i,1} = { every level-1 code present in the table } (|S| = k_1 <= 256). For l >= 2: S_{i,l} = { (par_l(i), k) : k is a level-l code that actually occurs under parent par_l(i) } (children of i's own parent; |S| <= 256, never the global 256, which is why deeper levels cannot degenerate into an item-identifier test). Denominator prototypes are the FULL barycentres B_pi' for pi' in S_{i,l}, pi' != pi_l(i); the own class uses q_{i,l}.

(6) Per-term source-conditioned log-probability, with reference scale sigma:
    sigma = median over all items i of d_c(u_i, v_i)   (one scalar from the frozen reference only; identical for all 97 tables, so it cannot be tuned per table).
    z_own = -d_c(u_i, q_{i,l})^2 / (2*sigma^2);
    z_pi' = -d_c(u_i, B_pi')^2 / (2*sigma^2) for pi' in S_{i,l}, pi' != pi_l(i);
    log p_{i,l} = z_own - logsumexp( {z_own} U {z_pi'} ).

(7) Informative support. T = { (i,1) : k_1 >= 2 } U { (i,l) : l >= 2 and |S_{i,l}| >= 2 }. A level that does not discriminate (parent with a single child) contributes no term, so an unused or duplicated level earns no free credit.

(8) THE METRIC (one scalar, higher is better):
    hyp_loo_sid_logprob = ( 1/|T| ) * sum_{(i,l) in T} log p_{i,l}      (nats per token, <= 0).
If T is empty the metric is defined as -log(C) = -log 256.
metrics.inputs: (a) the exported SID table: one integer code per (item, level), N = 24587, C = 256, L levels; (b) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference: per-item source vector u_i, per-item target vector v_i, ball radius R (hence c), and nothing else. No training split needed, no pairs, no labels, no recall, no Stage 2 or Stage 3 run.
metrics.geometry: The construction lives on the Poincare ball of constant curvature K = -1/R^2, c = 1/R^2: (i) d_c is the geodesic distance, not a Euclidean norm; (ii) every class prototype B_pi is a hyperbolic Frechet/Karcher barycentre obtained by Riemannian gradient flow, not an arithmetic mean; (iii) the leave-one-out prototype uses the Riemannian exp and log maps at B_pi (the correction log_{B_pi}(v_i)/(n_pi-1) is a tangent vector that the exp map wraps back onto the manifold). Curvature enters three times and is not removable: replacing d_c by Euclidean distance and exp/log by the identity changes all three steps (barycentres become centroids, the LOO correction becomes a linear shift, the Gaussian kernel changes shape). In the flat limit c -> 0 the metric collapses to a Euclidean centroid-classifier log-likelihood and its value changes.
metrics.why: Stage 3 decodes the target SID token by token from the SOURCE item with a beam of 10; Recall@10 is high exactly when the true code at each step is among the highest-probability codes given the source. This metric is the average per-token log-probability of the true code under a curvature-faithful, source-conditioned prototype classifier whose own prototype has had the item itself removed. What it adds over Q_H: Q_H is a SYMMETRIC target-side level-1 neighbourhood purity and collapses at levels 2-3 because the prefix becomes an item identifier that is trivially pure. This one is ASYMMETRIC (source u_i -> target-derived code prototypes B_pi), SEQUENTIAL (one term per decoding step, conditioned on the actual parent), CHANCE-NORMALISED by the softmax over the actually competing sibling set (so it keeps discriminating at levels 2 and 3 instead of saturating), and LEAVE-ONE-OUT (a table cannot score well by giving each item its own cell, because the item is deleted from its own prototype before the likelihood is taken). The LOO step is exactly the distinction between "the code memorises the item" and "the code is predictable from the source" - i.e. between a table that names items and one that geometrically organises them; only the latter generalises to unseen test pairs, which is what Recall@10 measures. A table whose source->code map is sharp and whose cells are curvature-round raises every z_own; a table whose cells cut across the reference's geodesic neighbourhoods lowers it.
metrics.compute: Barycentres: 256 level-1 groups plus at most 24587 prefixes per deeper level, each with <= 100 Karcher iterations over its own members, total <= 100 * 3 * 24587 ~ 7.4M log/exp evaluations. Scoring: for each item and level at most |S| <= 256 Poincare distances, so <= 3 * 24587 * 256 ~ 1.9e7 distance evaluations, plus 24587 exp/log calls for the LOO correction. All operations vectorise over items within a level (numpy/torch): a few seconds, well under 60 s, with at most 3 * 24587 * d floats of prototype storage (~6 MB at d = 64).
metrics.risks: (a) Scale mismatch: sigma = median_i d_c(u_i,v_i) is the reference's own source-target geodesic scale; if the towers are globally offset, sigma is too small and every softmax saturates at p ~ 1 (all tables near 0), or if too large all p ~ 1/|S| (no variance). Because sigma is pre-registered from the reference, this appears as compression of the 97 scores, not as overfitting. (b) If the reference keeps source and target vectors in different balls or applies a per-modality offset, d_c(u_i, B_pi) is not meaningful; a per-item constant offset cancels inside each softmax, a code-dependent offset does not. (c) Very skewed parent sizes: one giant parent dominates the deeper-level terms. (d) Karcher means in sparse or crescent-shaped cells may hit the iteration cap; the last iterate is used, so it stays deterministic but slightly biased. (e) The LOO prototype is only first-order exact; for n_pi = 2 or 3 the correction moves far and may exit a badly conditioned cell. (f) One bad deep level only lowers the average, so an otherwise excellent table can be under-ranked.
metrics.failure_mode: Worst on a SID table whose level-1 codes are assigned at random with respect to the reference geometry (codes hashed from the item id, or level-1 codes permuted across cells): every B_pi becomes a mixture of geodesically unrelated targets, u_i is roughly equidistant from its own and all competing barycentres, all z are near equal, and every log p_{i,l} sits at its chance value -log|S_{i,l}| (about -log 256 at level 1), driving the mean to the floor. Also worst on a maximally fine, geometry-blind enumeration: 256 arbitrary level-1 buckets each split into near-singleton level-2/level-3 codes, so after LOO deletion the own prototype reverts to the parent mixture while competing sibling prototypes sit on individual target vectors, making the true code no more likely than its siblings. It does NOT collapse on a table that gives every item a unique level-3 code with a geometrically coherent level 1 and 2 - exactly where Q_H's level-3 term saturates and stops discriminating.
